clue.text: Daughter's motoring club going over Tesla's facts and figures

indicators.note: to go over something is to straddle it, so one piece sits astride another

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring club
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: A daughter's breakdown club is poring over statistics about Tesla cars.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car maker, but here it is the physics unit, symbol T. The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a roadside rescue club.
explanation.definitionFit: Data is the collective term for gathered information and numerical records, exactly what facts and figures describes.

clue.text: Furious when flower head is knocked off by branches

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its opening letter

blocks.note: the lupin is a tall garden flower
the arms of a river or tree are its branches

explanation.surface: A gardener is livid that low branches have snapped the top off a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The beheaded lupin leaves UPIN, which joins ARMS to give UP IN ARMS.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up in arms is an idiom for being angrily protesting, hence intensely angry or outraged.

clue.text: No huge labour to make a sufficient quantity

indicators.note: to labour material is to work it over, so the letters are worked into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: No great effort is needed to produce an adequate amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' reads as a noun for effort, but it works as a verb telling you to rework the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Enough is used as a pronoun meaning as much as is required, an adequate amount or measure.

clue.text: Judge new bishop in old Yorkshire city to be an archetypal Englishman

indicators.note: something placed in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
O is the abbreviation for old
N is the abbreviation for new
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Hull is a port city in East Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A judge appoints a new bishop to an ancient Yorkshire see, the very model of an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' is not part of the city's name: it is O, standing before HULL, which takes in N and B after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: John Bull is the stout cartoon figure personifying England, a national caricature like America's Uncle Sam.

clue.text: A bride's unhappy with such a mattress

definitions.note: 'such a mattress' points back to the wordplay: the mattress the jumbled letters make

indicators.note: an unhappy state is a disturbed one, so the letters are upset into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newlywed is disappointed to find the marriage bed is an inflatable one.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue tells a little story, and the definition only makes sense once you see the bride's letters rearranged into the mattress.
explanation.definitionFit: An air bed is an inflatable mattress, the type described once the letters of the wordplay are rearranged.

clue.text: Drift in and out of sleep as 12 noon slips away

definitions.text: Drift in and out of sleep

indicators.note: whatever slips away is no longer there, so a letter goes missing

blocks.note: the number written as the word for a set of twelve
N is an abbreviation for noon, as in 12 n.

explanation.surface: Someone nods off on and off through the midday hour.
explanation.walkthrough: '12 noon' looks like one time of day, but 12 is a number to be written as a word and noon is the letter removed from it.
explanation.definitionFit: To doze is to sleep lightly and fitfully, slipping in and out of wakefulness.

clue.text: Charlie's copying Mike in holidaying under canvas

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so a letter is inserted

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
aping is imitating
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie imitates his friend Mike on a tent holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie and Mike look like two campers, but they are radio-alphabet letters; M goes inside APING after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Camping means staying in tents, and canvas is the traditional tent fabric, so holidaying under canvas describes it.

clue.text: Keep an eye on reptile

blocks.note: first meaning: to watch over or observe
second meaning: a large lizard of Africa, Asia and Australia

explanation.surface: Watch out for the lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a warning about a dangerous creature; the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to observe and check over time; as a noun it names a family of big lizards.

clue.text: Jackdaw nest concealed when day breaks

definitions.note: a phrase for the time of day, standing for the noun naming that moment

indicators.note: what is concealed is tucked away inside other words, out of plain sight

blocks.note: the end of the bird's name runs into the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A jackdaw's nest is tucked away out of sight at first light.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is daybreak, the first appearance of morning light, so it is the moment when day breaks.

clue.text: French articles about catch thrown back by sailor not based on facts

indicators.note: something thrown back is sent the opposite way, so the word runs backwards
about means surrounding, so the outer words go around the rest

blocks.note: un and le are French for 'a' and 'the'
to net is to catch
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A French report on a sailor's returned catch is pure fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The two French articles do not sit together: one opens the answer and the other closes it, wrapping the rest. AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An untenable position cannot be defended or maintained, typically because the evidence does not support it.

clue.text: Shocking art movement has a following — I'm not sure about it on reflection

indicators.note: movement shifts things into new positions, so the letters change places
pieces following one another are placed in sequence
a reflection shows things backwards, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: taken as written
um is a hesitant noise of uncertainty
taken as written
c, short for circa, means about
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scandalous new art movement has fans, but the critic is doubtful when thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art movement' looks like Cubism or Dada; it means rearrange ART. C is circa, the dating abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Traumatic describes something deeply distressing, which is the adjectival sense of shocking.

clue.text: Guiding light from church on hill

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A beacon shines from a church on a hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, church 'on' hill means it comes after the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a handheld lamp or burning brand carried to show the way, so it serves as a light for guidance.

clue.text: Clan's brief attempt to live on island

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the word loses its final letter
placed on something here means following it, so the piece named first is placed second

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
I is the abbreviation for island
to be is to exist, to live

explanation.surface: A clan makes a short-lived effort to settle on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' is the verb to exist, not lively; the order is set by 'on', which sends it after the island.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribe is a social group bound by kinship and shared ancestry, which is just what a clan is.

clue.text: Quietly left off plaque with date incorrectly cut for watercourse

indicators.note: letters taken off are removed from the word
something done incorrectly comes out in the wrong order

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for date
taken as written

explanation.surface: A memorial plaque was quietly abandoned because its date was carved wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like the carving of the plaque, but it is anagram fodder along with D; P and L both come off plaque.
explanation.definitionFit: An aqueduct is a channel or bridge built to carry water, a man-made course for flowing water.

clue.text: Small boat's old with bamboo frame

indicators.note: a frame surrounds what it holds, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: bamboo is a cane
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A little boat is ancient and built on a bamboo framework.
explanation.walkthrough: The bamboo frame is CANE, holding O between its N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light narrow boat paddled by hand, a modest vessel rather than a ship.

clue.text: Fasteners for flies?

blocks.note: first meaning: toothed closures on clothing and bags
second meaning: speeds along, moves very quickly

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the fastenings on trouser flies; read 'flies' as a verb and it means rushes about.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word names slide fasteners; as a verb it means moves at great speed, darting along.

clue.text: Approached large animal

blocks.note: came, as in came near
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big beast drew near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large animal' looks like one phrase, but large belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The camel is a humped desert mammal, a specific example of the general class creature.

clue.text: Casino worker's cough getting worse?

blocks.note: surface reading: a casino employee whose chesty cough is deteriorating
setter's reading: a comparative adjective made from the barking cough of children, meaning more afflicted by it

explanation.surface: A gaming-table dealer's chesty cough is deteriorating.
explanation.walkthrough: Croup is a barking childhood cough; treat it as if it took the comparative ending of an adjective, and 'more croupy' becomes the dealer's job title.
explanation.definitionFit: A croupier runs a gaming table, raking in chips and paying out bets at roulette or cards.

clue.text: Models have little space in marquee

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car, so two of them give two Ts
an en is a small printer's space

explanation.surface: Fashion models get very little room inside a party marquee.
explanation.walkthrough: Models look like catwalk people, but they are Model T Fords; an en is a printer's half-width space.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquee is a large tent used for outdoor events, so the general shelter word covers it.

clue.text: Large number finally get short time on beach

indicators.note: finally points to the end of a word, keeping its closing letter
something short is cut down, so the word loses its tail

blocks.note: the last letter of get
an hour is a unit of time
a beach is made of sand

explanation.surface: Crowds at last manage a brief spell on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large number' reads as the crowd on the beach, but it is the definition; 'time' cut short loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand is ten hundreds, a big round figure, so it is a fair example of a high number.

clue.text: Sent for a trip along the esplanade

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters fall over into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was dispatched for an outing by the promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' reads as an outing to the coast, but it means the preceding letters stumble into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a level walkway by the shore, the seaside promenade that a sea front is.

clue.text: City of London finance assumed to be productive

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on board, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: to fund is to finance
EC is the postcode district of the City of London

explanation.surface: The Square Mile's money is taken for granted as profitable.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London is the financial district, whose postcodes begin EC; 'assumed' means taken in, not supposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fecund means fertile and capable of producing much, whether offspring, crops or ideas.

clue.text: Bashed in first of stakes to dishearten vampire

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter
removing the heart takes out the middle, keeping only the outer letters

blocks.note: the opening letter of stakes
taken as written
the outside letters of vampire

explanation.surface: A vampire hunter drives in stakes to demoralise a vampire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bashed in' sounds like the action of the stake, but it is the definition: stove is a past tense of stave in.
explanation.definitionFit: To stave in is to smash a hole in something; its past form, alongside staved, is stove.

clue.text: Stay outside and check procedure

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its two ends

blocks.note: the end letters of stay
to stem a flow is to check it

explanation.surface: Wait outdoors and verify the process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' means stop, as in stemming bleeding, not verify.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an organised method or set of rules for doing something, the same as a procedure.

clue.text: Bags of support with crowds

blocks.note: to back is to support
to pack a place is to crowd it

explanation.surface: Lots of backing from large crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags of' reads as slang for plenty; Bags alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Backpacks are rucksacks, carrying sacks with shoulder straps, so they are a kind of luggage.

clue.text: Degree students have big party

blocks.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
L is a learner, so two of them are students

explanation.surface: Graduates celebrate with a huge bash.
explanation.walkthrough: L is a learner, from the L-plates on a British learner driver's car; two learners make students.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a grand formal dance, a large social gathering with music, so it is a big celebration.

clue.text: Smell extremely bad odour around layabout

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters
turned around means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the end letters of smell
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A dreadful whiff hangs about an idle lounger.
explanation.walkthrough: BO is the standard abbreviation for body odour.
explanation.definitionFit: A slob is a lazy, untidy person who idles about, a synonym for an idler.

clue.text: Cattle cross east between beginning of October and November

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter
what lies between two things is flanked by them, so the pair go round it

blocks.note: the opening letter of October
a cross is the shape X
E is the abbreviation for east
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Livestock move eastward in the autumn, between October and November.
explanation.walkthrough: November is a radio-alphabet word for N, not the month; only October is cut to its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxen are domesticated bovines, especially castrated bulls used for draught, so they are livestock of that kind.

clue.text: Wrap boy's broken ankle with some kind of shirt

indicators.note: broken things are smashed apart and pieced together differently

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for boy
taken as written
a T-shirt is one kind of shirt

explanation.surface: Bandage a lad's fractured ankle using a strip of his shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrap' looks like the first aid instruction, but it is the definition as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A blanket is a covering you wrap around yourself, and wrap as a noun means a shawl or covering.

clue.text: Average kind of wine knocked back causes wind

indicators.note: knocked back means sent backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the mean is an average
red is a kind of wine

explanation.surface: Downing ordinary plonk gives you flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests drinking the wine, and 'wind' suggests gas; read wind to rhyme with find, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to follow a twisting, turning course, as a river does, which is what winding means.
